newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate up after previous day's late dip.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate up after previous day's late dip.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were trading 180 basis points higher at 17.40 percent in late morning dealing on Tuesday.
Dealers said rates had returned to average trading levels for the prior session after a late dip they said was driven by speculation.
"Yesterday you had far more deals settled at around 17.00 percent than the closing rate of 15.70 percent, so today the market has gone back to Monday's dealing range," a fixed-income analyst said.
Dealers said early weakness by the peso, whose 48-hour benchmark contract was 0.1 centavos softer at 7.7990/7.8020 per dollar, had also contributed to the early rise in secondary market rates.
Overnight rates on bank paper were up 100 basis points at 19.00 percent.

Liquidity of 261 million pesos was scheduled to return to the system from a central bank operation on Monday. Dealers also expected a liquidity inflow of 200 million pesos in cash and a further 400 million pesos in government spending.
